canonical_title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.3 for coding and agentic workflows
treatment: Covered as a model release. Reinclude only for max-reasoning availability, material pricing/model-card changes, open-weight release, major independent evaluations, or production adoption/breakage.
known_facts: Meta released Muse Spark 1.3 with improved coding and agentic-task performance and is rolling it out in Muse Code and Meta Model API.
Existing reasoning modes are available at launch; a max-reasoning version is planned after additional safety testing.
Meta says the model is better at long-horizon work, managing multiple workflows in a long thread, generating context with tools, correcting gaps in plans and tracking learned information.
Meta kept API pricing unchanged from Muse Spark 1.2.
Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said the update is intended to support future personal agents, while Meta said it did not pause development but increased safety and alignment investment.
Meta's published benchmark claims include strong coding and long-context results; these remain vendor-reported pending broader independent replication.
reinclude_only_if: Meta releases the max-reasoning variant or materially changes availability or pricing.
Meta publishes Muse Spark open weights or a materially revised license/model card.
Independent reproducible evaluations materially alter the interpretation of coding, agentic, long-context, or cost performance.
Muse Spark 1.3 reaches major consumer surfaces or experiences a material regression, outage, or safety incident.
Meta releases the larger next-generation Muse model in a way that supersedes this topic.
notes: NEW for the 2026-09-03 Midday window. Mark Zuckerberg's launch post was timestamped Sep 2 3:26 PM ET = Sep 3 04:26 JST, after the prior Night boundary.
